subject: Moving repeat calculations to transformed parameters

messages.author: fac328645a1ff2dd
messages.subject: Moving repeat calculations to transformed parameters
parts:
I'm working on a non-linear model that has some parts that repeat across the formula.
Is it possible in brms to specify that this repeat part should be calculated in transformed parameters (in order to avoid re-calculating it over and over)?

For instance, the following model works, but results in unnecessary computations of F(aSelf, l_prior, wSelf) + F(aOthers, l_sensory, wOthers). In this case it's only twice, but the model might be expanded to have even more repeats.

  circular_f = bf(
     l_confidence ~ bias +
       F(0, l_prior   + F(aSelf, l_prior, wSelf) + F(aOthers, l_sensory, wOthers), wSelf) +
       F(0, l_sensory + F(aSelf, l_prior, wSelf) + F(aOthers, l_sensory, wOthers), wOthers),
    bias + wSelf + wOthers + aSelf + aOthers ~ 1 + (1|p|Participant),
   nl = TRUE)
   


The resulting stancode is then:

model {
    mu[n] = mu_bias[n] + F(0 , C_1[n] + F(mu_aSelf[n] , C_1[n] , mu_wSelf[n]) + F(mu_aOthers[n] , C_2[n] , mu_wOthers[n]) , mu_wSelf[n]) + F(0 , C_2[n] + F(mu_aSelf[n] , C_1[n] , mu_wSelf[n]) + F(mu_aOthers[n] , C_2[n] , mu_wOthers[n]) , mu_wOthers[n]);
}

but I would like it to instead be something like this:

transformed parameters {
    vector[N] I = F(mu_aSelf[n] , C_1[n] , mu_wSelf[n]) + F(mu_aOthers[n] , C_2[n] , mu_wOthers[n]);
}

model {
    mu[n] = mu_bias[n] + F(0 , C_1[n] + I[n] , mu_wSelf[n]) + F(0 , C_2[n] + I[n] , mu_wOthers[n]) , mu_wOthers[n]);
}


I can of course manually change the stancode and put it back in the brmsfit object, but this feels less elegant than it could be.
So is there any way to do this directly in brms? It could look something like:

circular_f2 = bf(
    l_confidence ~ bias +
        F(0, l_prior   + I, wSelf) +
        F(0, l_sensory + I, wOthers),
    I = F(aSelf, l_prior, wSelf) + F(aOthers, l_sensory, wOthers),
    bias + wSelf + wOthers + aSelf + aOthers ~ 1 + (1|p|Participant),
    nl = TRUE)

Here's a reprex. The crucial part is the two bf() formulas I quoted above but I figure context is always helpful.
https://gist.github.com/maltelau/cb53b4e7afcc33ee22b1f171662c1480

messages.subject: Re: Moving repeat calculations to transformed parameters
parts:
I realize now that actually most of the model block would have to be moved to transformed parameters since I need some of the other paramters (mu_wSelf etc) in calculating I.
When I move the whole thing (except priors and likelihood of course), it seems to work (although I don't know if it lead to any speedups yet, it's quite slow as is)

As far as I know, calculations in transformed parameters are less expensive because they're only evaluated once per iteration instead of the once per proposed transition that expressions in the model block are evaluated. Source? Probably betancourt somewhere on the net.
Am I mixing things up?
I guess in most glm-style models the issue is so small that it barely matters compared to other parts of the program, but intuitively it could make a difference in a model like this.

Of course, the price is also that now I have to filter out all the intermediates (mu_wSelf[1..N] etc) from the output ...

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Re: Moving repeat calculations to transformed parameters
parts:
I just implemented nested non-linear formulas on github.

It wasn't actually too complicated, because the internal structure was already prepared for it mostly.

Once you have installed the dev version you can fit your model using the following model specification:

circular_f2 = bf(
  l_confidence ~ bias +
    F(0, l_prior   + I, wSelf) +
    F(0, l_sensory + I, wOthers),
bias + wSelf + wOthers + aSelf + aOthers ~ 1 + (1|p|Participant),

nlf(I ~ F(aSelf, l_prior, wSelf) + F(aOthers, l_sensory, wOthers)),
  nl = TRUE
) + gaussian()

The only special thing is that you wrap the formula for I in nlf() so that brms knows its non-linear. nlf() existed before but
was not allowed to express nested non-linear formulas.
